title: Grading of free Lie algebras and homogeneous relation ideals
statement:
Let $X$ be a set, let $\Gamma$ be an abelian group written additively, and let $d:X\to\Gamma$ be a map. Work over $\mathbf Q$ with the Lie algebra and Lie ideal conventions of [def-wf-lie-algebra]. Let $F$ be the free rational Lie algebra on symbols $x$ indexed by $X$: every map from $X$ to a rational Lie algebra extends uniquely to a Lie homomorphism from $F$. A bracket word is a nonempty fully bracketed word in the symbols $x$; give it degree equal to the sum of the $d(x)$ of its letters, counted with repetitions. Let $F_\gamma$ be the rational linear span in $F$ of the bracket words of degree $\gamma$. Then
$$F=\bigoplus_{\gamma\in\Gamma}F_\gamma,\qquad [F_\gamma,F_\delta]\subseteq F_{\gamma+\delta}.$$
Here direct sum means that every element has a unique finite decomposition into elements of the displayed subspaces. Let $(s_t)_{t\in T}$ be any family with $s_t\in F_{\sigma_t}$ for specified $\sigma_t\in\Gamma$, and let $J$ be the Lie ideal generated by the $s_t$. Then $J=\bigoplus_\gamma(J\cap F_\gamma)$. More explicitly, $J\cap F_\gamma$ is spanned by
$$\operatorname{ad}(w_1)\cdots\operatorname{ad}(w_r)s_t,\qquad r\ge0,\quad \deg w_1+\cdots+\deg w_r+\sigma_t=\gamma,$$
where the $w_j$ are homogeneous bracket words and $\operatorname{ad}(w)z=[w,z]$. Consequently, for the quotient map $q:F\to F/J$, the subspaces $q(F_\gamma)$ form a direct-sum Lie grading and the induced map $F_\gamma/(J\cap F_\gamma)\to q(F_\gamma)$ is a vector-space isomorphism. These statements allow degree zero and negative degrees, relations equal to zero, and empty sets $X$ or $T$.

proof.text: Let $S\subseteq F$ be the rational span of all bracket words. Bilinearity shows $[S,S]\subseteq S$: expand two finite sums, and each bracket of two words is again a word. Thus $S$ is a Lie subalgebra in [def-wf-lie-algebra] containing every generator. By the free universal property in the hypothesis, the generator map $X\to S$ extends to $f:F\to S$. The inclusion $i:S\to F$ makes $if$ and $\operatorname{id}_F$ homomorphisms agreeing on $X$, so uniqueness gives $if=\operatorname{id}_F$. Therefore $S=F$. Grouping a finite word expansion by its degrees proves that the $F_\gamma$ span $F$. Expanding brackets in two such homogeneous expansions gives $[F_\gamma,F_\delta]\subseteq F_{\gamma+\delta}$, since the degree of the bracket of two words is the sum of their degrees.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-loop-lie-finite-support-model] with $L=F$ and this $\Gamma$. Write $C=\mathbf Q[\Gamma]\otimes_{\mathbf Q}F$ and $\Theta:C\to\Gamma\to_0F$ for its Lie algebra and linear model. Freeness supplies a Lie homomorphism $D:F\to C$ with $D(x)=e_{d(x)}\otimes x$. Induct on the construction of a bracket word $w$. For a letter this is the defining equation of $D$. If $w=[u,v]$, the induction hypotheses and the cited tensor-bracket formula give
$$D(w)=[e_{\deg u}\otimes u,e_{\deg v}\otimes v]=e_{\deg u+\deg v}\otimes[u,v].$$
Consequently $D(w)=e_{\deg w}\otimes w$ for every word. By linearity, for every $a\in F_\gamma$ one has $D(a)=e_\gamma\otimes a$ and $\Theta D(a)=\operatorname{single}_\gamma(a)$. This remains valid when a word evaluates to zero.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, printed p.504 (PDF p.516), homogeneous-presentation prerequisite; the argument below is supplied by Q11, not asserted to be Milne's proof. Mathlib loop-algebra model as cited in step 2.

proof.text: For a finite set $B\subseteq\Gamma$ suppose $a_\gamma\in F_\gamma$ and $\sum_{\gamma\in B}a_\gamma=0$. Apply the linear map $\Theta D$ of step 2 and use the singleton equation in [lem-sfb-loop-lie-finite-support-model]. The resulting equality is $\sum_{\gamma\in B}\operatorname{single}_\gamma(a_\gamma)=0$ in the space of finitely supported functions. Evaluation at any $\delta\in B$ gives $a_\delta=0$. Any two finite decompositions differ by such a relation after taking the union of their supports; hence they agree. Together with step 1 this proves the direct-sum grading of $F$. No order or positivity on the degree group was used.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, printed p.504 (PDF p.516), homogeneous-presentation prerequisite; the argument below is supplied by Q11, not asserted to be Milne's proof. Mathlib loop-algebra model as cited in step 2.

proof.text: Let $V$ be the rational span of all $\operatorname{ad}(w_1)\cdots\operatorname{ad}(w_r)s_t$ with $r\ge0$ and each $w_j$ a bracket word, with no degree restriction yet. The case $r=0$ puts all $s_t$ in $V$. For any $a\in F$, write $a$ as a finite linear combination of words by step 1. For each spanning vector $v=\operatorname{ad}(w_1)\cdots\operatorname{ad}(w_r)s_t$, the expansion of $[a,v]$ is a linear combination of the same kind, obtained by prepending one word. Expanding also in $v$ proves $[F,V]\subseteq V$. Thus $V$ is an ideal by [def-wf-lie-algebra], and minimality of the ideal generated by the $s_t$ gives $J\subseteq V$. Conversely every ideal containing all $s_t$ contains these iterated brackets, by induction on $r$, and their rational span; in particular $V\subseteq J$. Hence $V=J$.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, printed p.504 (PDF p.516), homogeneous-presentation prerequisite; the argument below is supplied by Q11, not asserted to be Milne's proof. Mathlib loop-algebra model as cited in step 2.

proof.text: Every spanning vector in step 4 belongs to $F_{\deg w_1+\cdots+\deg w_r+\sigma_t}$ by the bracket rule of step 1. Given $z\in J$, expand it as a finite linear combination of those vectors and group terms of equal degree. Each grouped term lies in $J\cap F_\gamma$, so $J$ is the sum of these intersections; directness follows from step 3. If moreover $z\in F_\gamma$, uniqueness in step 3 forces every grouped term of degree different from $\gamma$ to be zero. The remaining group expresses $z$ as a span of exactly the iterated brackets with total degree $\gamma$. This proves the stated formula for $J\cap F_\gamma$, including zero relations with any assigned degree.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, printed p.504 (PDF p.516), homogeneous-presentation prerequisite; the argument below is supplied by Q11, not asserted to be Milne's proof. Mathlib loop-algebra model as cited in step 2.

proof.text: Use the quotient bracket $[q(a),q(b)]=q([a,b])$ from [def-wf-lie-algebra]. Thus $[q(F_\gamma),q(F_\delta)]\subseteq q(F_{\gamma+\delta})$, and the $q(F_\gamma)$ span $F/J$ by step 1. To prove directness, lift a finite relation $\sum_\gamma q(a_\gamma)=0$, with $a_\gamma\in F_\gamma$, to $\sum_\gamma a_\gamma\in J$. Step 5 and uniqueness of the grading of $F$ imply $a_\gamma\in J\cap F_\gamma$ for every degree, so every summand $q(a_\gamma)$ vanishes. Finally the linear map $F_\gamma/(J\cap F_\gamma)\to q(F_\gamma)$ sends the class of $a$ to $q(a)$. It is well defined because differences in $J\cap F_\gamma$ map to zero, and surjective by the definition of the image. If $q(a)=0$ then $a\in J\cap F_\gamma$, so its kernel is zero. Its inverse sends $q(a)$ to the class of any lift $a\in F_\gamma$; two such lifts differ by $J\cap F_\gamma$, proving independence of the lift and linearity. This gives the required vector-space isomorphism.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, printed p.504 (PDF p.516), homogeneous-presentation prerequisite; the argument below is supplied by Q11, not asserted to be Milne's proof. Mathlib loop-algebra model as cited in step 2.

proof.text: All expansions above are finite, regardless of the size of $X$, $T$ or $\Gamma$. If $X=\varnothing$, step 1 gives $F=0$ because there are no nonempty words; hence all conclusions reduce to zero spaces. If $T=\varnothing$, the spanning set in step 4 is empty and $J=0$. Zero and negative degrees, and collisions of degrees in a group with torsion, merely combine terms in the same finite group of summands and affect none of the coordinate or quotient arguments.
